name: Hundred
long_description:
Hundred is an automated inspection system for the components that make up devices like phones, smartwatches, and laptops. Hundred helps factories cut waste and prevent line-down issues by catching sub-100µm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line. 

Designs change so fast that traditional machine vision can't keep up, forcing factories to rely on manual inspection, literally people checking parts under microscopes to sort out bad parts. Human inspectors miss roughly 15% of defects, and a single bad part can turn a finished device into scrap. Hundred is replacing manual inspection with an imaging rig that scans an entire shipping tray of parts at once. 

The Hundred rig blocks ambient light and uses varied controlled lighting configurations to detect defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials. The controlled environment means Hundred only needs to scan a single good part before it can find defects, categorize them, and assess their severity accurately.

Defects cost U.S. discrete manufacturers $45 billion a year, a problem Hundred's CEO, Erica, saw firsthand as a mechanical engineer designing devices at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap. She met Imani, Hundred's CPO, at Columbia University's admitted-students day in 2017 and Imani went on to spend five years at Twitch building software that handles billions of requests a day. Erica later met Iris, Hundred's CTO, in the Bay Area. Iris worked as a quant at Citadel before pivoting to study at Imperial College London where she researched machine learning on 3D meshes and other structured data. Together, they're building Hundred because manual inspection shouldn't still exist in 2026.

launches.title: Hundred: Automated inspection for precision hardware parts
launches.tagline: Catch sub-100μm visual defects before parts reach the assembly line
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re[ Erica](https://www.linkedin.com/in/erica-diaz1/),[ Iris](https://www.linkedin.com/in/iris-liao-03b041152/), and[ Imani](https://www.linkedin.com/in/imani-gosserand/), co-founders of[ Hundred](https://hundred.systems/) 

Hundred replaces the typical human visual inspection done on precision hardware parts with an automated system that can scan a whole shipping tray of parts at once.

<https://youtu.be/xC9_YnK2PJc>

**The Problem**

Small part designs change too fast for traditional machine vision to keep up, so factories still inspect parts by hand: literally people with microscopes sorting out bad parts. As manufacturers move away from China to the US or India, operators familiar with common defects don’t move with them. While trained operators miss \~15% of defects, untrained operators miss even more. 

One bad part can turn a finished product into scrap material and more than 3 bad parts in an hour can stop the assembly line. Defects cost U.S. manufacturers $45B a year, and line downtime costs another $245B.

**What we’re building**

Hundred eliminates human subjectivity by imaging parts at mass production volumes, right in their shipping trays. A full tray can be placed in the Hundred rig, which detects defects smaller than 100µm on a range of materials and finishes. Where human inspectors might require a month of training, Hundred can stop defects on Day 1.

**Our goal is to make sure engineers can set their specs once and know that part quality will hold up when they leave the factory.**

**The Team**

**Erica** designed and ramped consumer hardware at Meta, Google, and Magic Leap for 5 years where she root-caused device failures to bad parts and drove vendors to fix them.

**Iris** was a Quantitative Researcher at Citadel. She then spent a year at Imperial College London researching ML on 3D meshes and other structured data.

**Imani** worked for 5 years at Twitch as a software engineer at the intersection of notifications, short-form content, and ML for hundreds of millions of streamers and viewers.

**Our Ask**

We’d love to connect with precision hardware companies and contract manufacturers who are struggling with part inspection or looking to scale their inspection capacity.

**Learn more at [hundred.systems](http://hundred.systems)**
